instruction: I want to color-code the section headings in my tutorial guidelines for better visual organization. Please change the text color of both 'Setting' and 'Assessment' headings to blue (any shade of blue) to distinguish them from the body text.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing text color of 2 section headings to blue (any shade). Evaluator counts paragraphs with non-black text color. Expected count: 2.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Evaluator does not verify that SPECIFIC headings ('Setting' and 'Assessment') were colored - it only counts ANY paragraphs with non-black text, allowing false positives if user colors any 2 random paragraphs

CRITICAL: Evaluator does not verify that the color is BLUE - it accepts any non-black color (red, green, yellow, etc.), directly contradicting the instruction requirement for 'blue (any shade of blue)'

CRITICAL: Incomplete coverage - instruction requires verifying both which text was colored (specific headings) AND what color was used (blue), but evaluator only checks count of colored paragraphs generically
Logic issue: Getter checks paragraph-level coloring but doesn't verify the paragraph content matches 'Setting' or 'Assessment' text
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Modify getter to check paragraph text content and verify it contains 'Setting' or 'Assessment' (case-insensitive match or exact match)

Add blue color validation: check that RGB color values have B component significantly higher than R and G (e.g., B > max(R,G) + threshold, or use HSV color space to check hue is in blue range ~180-270 degrees)
Consider two-part verification: (1) identify paragraphs containing 'Setting'/'Assessment' text, (2) verify those specific paragraphs have blue-range color applied
Alternative: Use text search to locate the specific heading paragraphs, then verify their color properties match blue spectrum
